title: Situation
summary: Zhou Mingrui verifies that Klein Moretti’s catastrophic head wound is rapidly healing, reconstructs the apparent gunshot scene, learns more about the Moretti family’s modest life in Tingen, and recalls the luck-enhancement ritual performed before his transmigration. He decides that repeating the ritual may be his best lead for returning home.
worldbuilding: The Moretti household is financially constrained, but Benson arranged a gas lamp so Klein could study for admission to Khoy University.
Loen uses coin-operated gas meters; a copper penny is presented as a basic unit of everyday currency.
King George III appears on the currency, grounding the scene in the Loen monarchy.
The apartment’s tenants share a communal bathroom and water costs are folded into rent.
mysteries: How did Klein survive a revolver shot through the temple, and why is the wound healing abnormally fast?
Where did the revolver come from, and was the original Klein’s death truly suicide?
What is the meaning of the notebook line about everyone dying?
Did Zhou Mingrui’s luck-enhancement ritual cause the transmigration?
ritualMemory: The recalled ritual uses four portions of local staple food placed at the four corners of the room.
The participant walks four counter-clockwise steps to form a square while invoking four honorific titles.
The fourth title contains “The Celestial Worthy of Heaven and Earth for Blessings,” an early high-value mystery anchor.
changes: Zhou Mingrui accepts that he is physically alive in Klein’s body.
He reconstructs the immediate physical evidence of Klein’s death.
He identifies the luck-enhancement ritual as his strongest hypothesis for transmigration and plans to repeat it.
